plain_words.what: We decided where the effort goes, and what to buy instead of build.
plain_words.decided: Subscriptions is the core and gets real design. Billing is bought (Stripe). Fulfilment is kept simple.
plain_words.assumed: Payments are worth buying, not building. Almost always true, and true here.
plain_words.riskiest: If subscriptions turns out to be the boring part, we will have spent our design budget in the wrong place.

classifications.rationale: G1 (grow active subscribers) is won or lost on how easily a household chooses and changes its weekly meals; no off-the-shelf subscription product models cut-offs, swaps and pauses the way we need, so this is the decisive core and gets a rich domain model.
classifications.future_direction: Stays core for the foreseeable future; menu-choice UX is the differentiator (bet B1)

classifications.rationale: Charging a card weekly is a solved problem (Stripe, commodity evolution); it moves no goal on its own, so buy the provider and keep our side a transaction script around the adapter.
classifications.future_direction: Remains generic; revisit only if we move to invoicing B2B customers

classifications.rationale: Packing and shipping must work but a competitor's box arrives just as well; supporting, active-record CRUD over boxes and picking lists, with a possible move to a WMS product later.
